lines.text: Sounds fake? It's true. Not round. Not lumpy. Actual cubes.
A single wombat can leave up to a hundred of them, every night.
lines.caption: A single wombat can leave up to 100 of them, every night.

lines.text: For years, nobody knew how it did that.
Then scientists looked inside a wombat's gut.
Its walls aren't equally stretchy. Some parts are stiff, some are soft. Squeeze through that, and you get corners.
Wombats leave the cubes on rocks and logs to mark their turf. And cubes don't roll away.
The research even won an Ig Nobel Prize.
